title: Feature/1960
summary: Adds **Find the Verse**, a new extension with a guessing game. Someone creates a game by picking a secret verse and writing one hint per chance; then a player taps verses in the reader to guess, and the game says whether the secret verse is earlier or later. Games are saved to your account, so you can play, edit, or delete them later.

links.label: Issue 1960: Port the "find this verse" game for the Bible stack

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use the button above, in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer (one section later uses a phone). If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If it looks like the old version, do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac).

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Games are saved to your account, so most tests need you signed in. Open **Settings** (the gear icon), choose to sign in, enter your email address, then type the code that arrives in your inbox. Use an inbox you can check.

setup.title: Install the Find the Verse extension
setup.body: Open the app's menu and go to **Extensions**. If **Find the Verse** isn't already under **Installed**, install it from **Available**. If you can't find **Find the Verse** at all, mark every test **Blocked** and say so in the note.

setup.title: Find the game button
setup.body: A new **Find the Verse** button (a crosshair / target icon) appears in the app's toolbar. If you don't see it, look in the toolbar's overflow (**...**) menu. Clicking it opens the game panel at the side of the screen. In these tests, "the panel" means that game panel.

setup.title: Use one English translation
setup.body: Read in an English translation such as **BSB** for every test, so the book names and verse text match what's written here.

sections.title: Creating a game
sections.intro: Make the game the later sections play: secret verse **John 3:16**, four chances.

tests.title: The panel starts with a Create a game button
steps: Click the **Find the Verse** toolbar button.
expected: A panel titled **Find the Verse** opens with a 🔍 icon, a short description of the game, and a **Create a game** button.
No **My saved games** list is shown yet (you haven't saved any).

tests.title: Saving an empty game shows one problem at a time
tests.why: The form checks the name first, then the secret verse, then the hints, and scrolls to whichever is wrong.
steps: Click **Create a game**.
Without filling anything in, click **Save game**.
Type `Test game` in **Game name** and click **Save game** again.
expected: After the first click, a red message **Give this game a name.** appears under the name box.
After the second click, the name message goes away and **Pick the secret verse before saving.** appears under **Secret verse** instead.
No game is saved and the panel stays on the **Create a game** form.

tests.title: Typing a reference picks the secret verse and opens it in the reader
tests.before: Continue on the form from the previous test.
steps: In the box with the placeholder `e.g. John 1:1`, type `John 3:16-17` and click **Go**.
Replace it with `Hezekiah 1:1` and press **Enter**.
Replace it with `John 3:16` and click **Go**.
expected: `John 3:16-17` shows **Pick a single verse, like John 1:1, not a range.**
`Hezekiah 1:1` shows **Couldn't recognise that reference. Try “John 1:1”.**
`John 3:16` shows a grey box reading **John 3:16** with the verse text in italics ("For God so loved the world…"), and the reader jumps to John chapter 3.

tests.title: Select from reader lets you pick the verse by tapping it
tests.why: The second way to choose a secret verse. The verse's normal toolbar gets an extra **Set as target** button, only while you're picking.
tests.before: Continue on the form. John 3:16 is the current secret verse.
steps: Click **Select from reader…**.
In the reader, click verse **John 3:3**.
In the toolbar that appears for the verse, click **Set as target**.
Type `John 3:16` in the reference box and click **Go** again, so the secret verse is back to John 3:16 for the rest of the tests.
expected: After **Select from reader…**, a coloured box says **Tap any verse in the reader, then choose Set as target in the toolbar.** with a **Cancel** button.
The verse toolbar shows a **Set as target** button (with a pin icon) alongside its usual buttons.
After **Set as target**, the coloured box goes away and the preview shows **John 3:3** with its text.
After the last step the preview shows **John 3:16** again.

tests.title: Every chance needs a hint, and you can add or remove chances
tests.why: Issue 1960 says hints are optional, but this PR requires a hint for every chance. Flag it if that's not what you expect.
steps: Look at the **Chances** section.
Click **Save game**.
Click the red **×** next to rows No. 5, 6 and 7 until only four rows are left.
Click **+ Add chance**, then click **×** on the new row.
Fill in the four hint boxes in order: `New Testament`, `One of the Gospels`, `Chapter 3`, `A very famous verse`. In the last one, press Enter once and type `second line` before you finish.
expected: At first there are seven empty hint rows, numbered 1 to 7, and the label reads **Chances (7)**.
Clicking **Save game** shows **Chance 1 is empty. Fill it in or delete it before saving.**
The label counts down as rows are removed, ending at **Chances (4)**; **+ Add chance** makes it 5, and removing that row brings it back to 4.
The last hint box grows to show both lines of text.
The red message disappears once all four hints are filled.

tests.title: Saving the game adds it to My saved games, and it survives a reload
tests.before: The form has name `Test game`, secret verse John 3:16, and four filled hints.
steps: Click **Save game**.
Look at the card under **My saved games**.
Click **Show reference** on the card.
Reload the page, then open the panel again from the toolbar button.
expected: The panel goes back to the start screen, and a **My saved games** list shows one card: **Test game**, a **Show reference** link, and **Saved game · 4 chances · <today's date>**, with a **Play** button and a **...** menu.
The reference is hidden until you click **Show reference**, which replaces the name with **John 3:16**.
After the reload the card is still there.

tests.title: Cancel throws a draft away without saving
steps: Click **Create a game**.
Type `Throwaway` as the name, then click **Cancel**.
Click **Create a game** again.
expected: **Cancel** returns to the start screen and no **Throwaway** card appears.
The new form is blank: empty name, no secret verse, seven empty hints.

sections.title: Playing a game
sections.intro: Play `Test game` (secret verse John 3:16, four chances). Order matters: each test continues the same round.

tests.title: Play starts a round at Genesis 1
steps: On the **Test game** card, click **Play**.
Click the round **?** button next to the chances count.
expected: The reader jumps to **Genesis 1**.
The panel shows **Test game**, a coloured pill reading **4 / 4 left**, a **?** button, the line **Tap any verse in the reader to guess.**, and an **End game** button.
Clicking **?** replaces it with the first hint: **New Testament**.

tests.title: A wrong book says later or earlier, greys out what's ruled out, and uses a chance
steps: Click verse **Genesis 1:1** in the reader.
Click **Genesis 1:1** again.
Open the book list (the book/chapter picker) and look at **Genesis**.
Click **?** to see the next hint.
expected: The normal verse toolbar does NOT appear when you click a verse; the click counts as a guess instead.
The panel says **The verse is later in the Bible — try a book further along.** and the pill shows **3 / 4 left**.
Clicking the same verse again shows the same message but does NOT use another chance (still **3 / 4 left**).
The verses of Genesis 1 look faded, and **Genesis** is greyed out in the book list.
The **?** button is back (a new chance means a new hint) and shows **One of the Gospels**.

tests.title: Guessing past the verse says it's earlier, and the reveal buttons unlock at half the chances
tests.why: With four chances, the reveal buttons appear after two guesses (half, rounded up).
steps: Use the book list to open **Revelation 1**.
Click verse **Revelation 1:1**.
expected: The panel says **The verse is earlier in the Bible — try a book further back.** and shows **2 / 4 left**.
**Revelation** is now greyed out in the book list, as well as Genesis.
Two new buttons appear: **Reveal hint** and **Reveal verse**.

tests.title: Right book and right chapter give their own messages, and the chapter list greys out ruled-out chapters
steps: Open **John 1** and click verse **John 1:1**.
Open the chapter list for John and look at chapter 1.
Open **John 3** and click verse **John 3:20**.
expected: After John 1:1: **Right book! The verse is in a later chapter.** and **1 / 4 left**. Chapter 1 is greyed out in John's chapter list.
After John 3:20: **Right chapter! The verse number is lower.** In John 3, verses 20 and after look faded.
The pill now reads **Out of chances** in red, with the message **You've used all your chances, but you can keep guessing — good luck!**

tests.title: Reveal hint blanks out about half the words of the verse
steps: Click **Reveal hint**.
expected: A box labelled **PARTIAL HINT** shows the verse with roughly half of its words replaced by `___`, in random places.
The **Reveal hint** button disappears; **Reveal verse** stays.

tests.title: Finding the verse shows the win screen with confetti
steps: Click verse **John 3:16**.
Click **Back to main menu**.
Click a verse in the reader.
expected: Confetti falls, then 🎉 **You found it!**, **John 3:16**, the verse text in italics, and **5 guesses**.
**Back to main menu** returns to the start screen with the **Test game** card.
The faded verses and greyed-out books and chapters are back to normal, and clicking a verse opens the normal verse toolbar again.

tests.title: Reveal verse shows the answer and dims the rest of the chapter
steps: Click **Play** on **Test game**.
Click **Genesis 1:1**, then open **Revelation 1** and click **Revelation 1:1**.
Click **Reveal verse**.
Click another verse in the reader.
expected: The round starts fresh at **4 / 4 left**, with nothing greyed out from the last round.
**Reveal verse** opens **John 3**, scrolls to verse 16, and keeps it lit while the rest of the chapter is dimmed.
The panel shows **John 3:16** with the full verse text and **Better luck next time — keep going!**
Clicking another verse does not count as a guess and does not open the normal verse toolbar.

tests.title: End game stops the round
tests.before: Continue from the revealed round in the previous test.
steps: Click **End game**.
Click a verse in the reader.
expected: The panel returns to the start screen.
The dimmed verses return to normal, and clicking a verse opens the normal verse toolbar.

tests.title: Closing the panel during a round shows a small bar over the reader
tests.why: On a phone the panel covers the reader, so the round has to keep going with the panel closed.
steps: Click **Play** on **Test game**, then close the panel.
Click verse **Genesis 1:1**.
Click **?** in the bar.
Click the **Find the Verse** toolbar button to reopen the panel, then close it again.
Click **End game** in the bar.
expected: A floating bar appears near the bottom of the reader with **Test game**, **4 / 4 left**, a **?** button, and **End game**.
After the guess, the bar shows **3 / 4 left** and **The verse is later in the Bible — try a book further along.**
**?** shows the hint for the current chance (**One of the Gospels**).
While the panel is open the bar is hidden; reopening it shows the same round in progress.
**End game** removes the bar, and clicking a verse opens the normal verse toolbar again.

tests.title: Edit changes the saved game instead of adding a copy
steps: On the **Test game** card, open the **...** menu and choose **Edit**.
Change the name to `Test game edited`, remove the last hint row, and click **Save game**.
expected: The form title reads **Edit game**, with the name, the John 3:16 preview, and all four hints filled in (the last one still showing both lines).
After saving there is still only one card: **Test game edited**, **3 chances**, with the original date.
It is still there after a reload.

tests.title: Delete asks first, and Cancel keeps the game
steps: On the card, open **...** and choose **Delete**.
Click **Cancel**.
Open **...** again, choose **Delete**, then click **Delete**.
Reload the page and open the panel.
expected: The card shows **Delete this game?** with **Delete** and **Cancel** buttons in place of **Play**.
**Cancel** puts the card back as it was.
**Delete** removes the card, and the **My saved games** heading disappears with it.
After the reload the game is still gone.

tests.title: Saved games stay on your account and follow you to another browser
steps: Create and save a new game: name `Second browser`, secret verse `Psalm 23:1`, two hints of your choice.
In a different browser (or a private/incognito window), open the preview, sign in with the same email, install **Find the Verse** if needed, and open the panel.
expected: The **Second browser** card appears there too, with **2 chances**.

sections.title: Signed out, phone, and dark mode

tests.title: Signed out, the game asks you to sign in to save
tests.why: There's no way to play a game without saving it first, so signed-out users can only fill in the form.
tests.before: Open the preview in a private/incognito window and don't sign in. Install **Find the Verse** from **Extensions** if it lets you; if it requires signing in, mark this test **Skip**.
steps: Open the panel and click **Create a game**.
Fill in a name, secret verse `John 1:1`, and every hint.
Click the main button at the bottom.
expected: No **My saved games** list is shown.
The main button reads **Sign in to save games** instead of **Save game**.
Clicking it shows the red message **Sign in to save games** and nothing is saved.

tests.title: On a phone, picking a verse and playing work with the panel closed
tests.before: On a phone (or a computer window made as narrow as it goes), signed in, with a saved game such as **Second browser**.
steps: Open the panel, click **Create a game**, then **Select from reader…**.
Close the panel.
Tap any verse, then tap **Set as target** in the verse toolbar.
Click **Cancel** to throw the draft away.
Tap **Play** on a saved game, close the panel, and tap a few verses to guess.
expected: With the panel closed, a bar over the reader says **Tap any verse in the reader, then choose Set as target in the toolbar.** with **Cancel**.
After **Set as target** the panel reopens by itself and shows the verse you picked.
During play, the bar shows the chances, **?**, the latest feedback, and **End game**, and doesn't cover the verses you need to tap or the app's bottom controls.
Nothing is cut off or runs off the side of the screen in the panel or the bar.

tests.title: Everything is readable in dark mode
steps: Switch the app to dark mode in **Settings**.
Look at the start screen, the **Create a game** form (including a red error message), a round in play (panel and bar), and the win screen.
expected: All text, boxes, buttons and the greyed-out books and chapters are readable against the dark background. Nothing shows as dark text on a dark box or a bright white box.

notCovered: Behaviour when loading, saving or deleting games fails on the server (the "Couldn't save that game" style messages). These are hard to trigger by hand and are covered by automated tests.
Old saved games from before game names existed. None exist outside development.
Other languages: the game's text is only written in English so far.
Issue 1960 describes Phase 1 as local only (no saving) and hints as optional. This PR saves games to your account and requires a hint for every chance; these tests follow what the PR does.
